channel.description: The RFTUV Briefing is a short AI news and tech news podcast from Reporting from the Uncanny Valley (RFTUV), built from reporting and analysis at rftuv.ai. In a few minutes: what changed, why it matters, and what to watch next, in plain language. A quick briefing on artificial intelligence, technology, culture, and power, reported by humans.

item.title: A Personal Agent in the Pentagon, a Compute Limit in Albany, and Flu Six Weeks Early
item.description:
A Personal Agent in the Pentagon, a Compute Limit in Albany, and Flu Six Weeks Early. Hosted by Noel.
WIRED reported on October 29, citing sources, that an Accenture contractor connected a personal Claude Code account to a production environment on NIPRNet, the Defense Department's unclassified network, which holds Controlled Unclassified Information and serves multiple intelligence agencies. The sources said the contractor shared his own login credentials, giving the agent administrative access to write and deploy code and set up cloud servers, that it operated for about two months, and that it appears to have transmitted passwords, login details, and a network map to a third-party website WIRED did not name. WIRED reported no indication that classified systems were accessed and does not establish that a known weakness in that service was exploited. Accenture told WIRED the allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit and that it complied with its legal and contractual obligations; the Defense Department declined to comment. Plus: State Senator Andrew Gounardes and Assemblymember Jordan Wright introduced a bill expanding the RAISE Act that would let New York limit computing power for risky AI models, covering companies spending more than $1 billion on AI development over three years, with quarterly reporting, 90-day risk assessments, annual audits, and penalties up to $1 million per day for a first violation and $3 million per day for later violations. It is a proposal, not a law. And influenza is prevalent and widespread in New York about six weeks ahead of schedule, with 3,526 laboratory-confirmed cases in the week ending October 17, up 19 percent and about 400 percent above the same period last year, and Orange, Putnam, Westchester, and Sullivan among the highest-count counties. Hosted by Noel.
Stories: - A personal AI agent allegedly given access to a Pentagon system (WIRED) - New York lawmakers propose letting the state limit compute for risky AI models (New York State Senate) - Flu arrives six weeks early in New York (New York State Department of Health)

item.title: Two Charged in Stockport, Beekman Ordered to Open a Sober Home, and GM Pays $220 Million
item.description:
Two Charged in Stockport, Beekman Ordered to Open a Sober Home, and GM Pays $220 Million. Hosted by Noel.
New York State Police charged Devin Mackey, 23, and Demetries Mackey, 21, both of Hudson, with attempted murder in connection with an October 20 shooting on Hill Street in Stockport that wounded a 44-year-old man, according to a Troop K press release dated October 29. Each faces the same charges, including two counts of endangering the welfare of a child, and a preliminary hearing was scheduled for today, October 30, at 11:00 a.m. in Town of Stockport Court. The charges are accusations and both men are presumed innocent until proven guilty. Plus: a federal judge signed a consent injunction requiring the Town of Beekman to allow a sober home for women, Hudson Valley Collective, to open, at first for up to four residents, while the United States' damages and classification claims remain pending. And General Motors will pay $220 million to settle attorneys general allegations that it sold driver behavior and location data from its Smart Driver program to data brokers who sold it to insurers, with $12,054,341 going to New York. Hosted by Noel.
Stories: - Two Hudson men charged with attempted murder in a Stockport shooting (June Mercer, RFTUV, from New York State Police) - A federal judge orders Beekman to let a sober home for women open (U.S. Attorney, Southern District of New York) - GM pays $220 million over driver data sold to insurers (New York Attorney General and coalition releases)

item.title: Utah Charges Kalshi, an Open Model Passes Cyber Tests, and Dutchess Halloween Curfews
item.description:
Utah Charges Kalshi, an Open Model Passes Cyber Tests, and Dutchess Halloween Curfews. Hosted by Noel.
Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed 14 criminal charges against KalshiEX LLC and its co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara, one day after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued to block Utah from enforcing its anti-gambling laws against the company. Both sides state their case in their own terms, and the charges carry a presumption of innocence. Plus: Z.AI's open-weight model GLM-5.3 completed 3 of 13 multi-stage cyberattack scenarios in controlled tests by AI security research firm Irregular, the strongest performance recorded from an openly available model, and in separate tests it broke the rules to reach correct answers, a behavior researchers call reward hacking. And in Dutchess County, no municipality has published official trick-or-treat hours for 2026, while four towns have Halloween curfews for unaccompanied minors in writing. Hosted by Noel.
Stories: - Utah charges Kalshi and its founders; the CFTC sues Utah back (Reuters) - An open-weight model passes cyber tests in controlled simulations (Reuters, reporting research by Irregular) - Halloween curfews in four Dutchess towns, and no official trick-or-treat hours (June Mercer, RFTUV)

item.title: Diggs Charged in Newburgh, Medicaid Fraud Sentences, and Alphabet Sinks on AI Bill
item.description:
Diggs Charged in Newburgh, Medicaid Fraud Sentences, and Alphabet Sinks on AI Bill. Hosted by Noel.
Newburgh city police have charged Carlos Diggs, 38, of Poughkeepsie, with first-degree robbery and second-degree criminal possession of a weapon in a gunpoint robbery reported October 22 on City Terrace, according to the Times Herald-Record as carried in the RFTUV blotter; detectives found a person matching the description on a scooter near First Street and Carpenter Avenue, he fled on foot through backyards and over fences after a stop attempt near Grand Street, and he was taken into custody near 114 First Street, where a detective recovered a 9-millimeter semi-automatic handgun. Court information and his attorney's name were not immediately available, and he is presumed innocent. Plus: New Windsor limo company owners Rohail Raja and Sharma Alam were sentenced in Orange County Court in a $3.4 million Medicaid fraud scheme, Raja to 6 to 18 years in prison and Alam to six months incarceration and five years probation, with $400,000 paid toward restitution and $3,034,730 remaining ordered; and Alphabet shares fell more than 10 percent after hours after third-quarter results showed revenue up 25 percent to $127.6 billion and Google Cloud revenue more than doubling, against $51.4 billion in capital expenditure and negative $9.07 billion free cash flow. Hosted by Noel.

Sharma Alam, 45, owner of SNR Limo Inc., sentenced to six months incarceration and five years probation on a fourth-degree conspiracy plea; forensic audit findings (billing for transports on dates and times when provider records show no visits occurred, and group trips billed as separate transports); April 15, 2020 to September 30, 2024; $3,434,730 admitted stolen; $400,000 paid at sentencing, $3,034,730 remaining ordered; May 14, 2026 company pleas (Unique Class Limo first-degree grand larceny, $2,666,634 admitted; capital expenditure $51.4 billion; free cash flow negative $9.07 billion, second straight negative quarter after a $5.9 billion outflow, itself the first negative reading in Alphabet's 22 years as a public company; item.title: Lawler and Conley Six Days Out, Fake Videos Target Senate Races, and a Dry Halloween
item.description:
Lawler and Conley Six Days Out, Fake Videos Target Senate Races, and a Dry Halloween. Hosted by Noel.
Six days before Election Day, both House party leaders have campaigned in New York's 17th Congressional District in the final week: House Speaker Mike Johnson was in Orangeburg, Rockland County, on October 27 for Rep. Mike Lawler, three days after House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries stumped for Democrat Cait Conley in Peekskill. Johnson estimated as much as $60 million will be spent in the district, which the Cook Political Report rates a toss-up. The Lawler campaign says a mailing from a group calling itself the American Forge Coalition arrived in district homes on October 23 and 24, says the group has no Federal Election Commission record and the mailing misstates Lawler's immigration position, and says it contacted the Department of Justice, which referred the matter to the FBI; campaign manager Ciro Riccardi has called on Conley to condemn the mailing, and the reporting notes the Conley campaign did not return calls and emails over two days. No source establishes who paid for the mailing. Plus: the Associated Press reports social media videos believed to be produced with AI and linked to Russia are misusing real people's names and photographs against Senate candidates Sherrod Brown in Ohio and James Talarico in Texas, with X takedowns trailing copies still online; and Halloween in the Hudson Valley is forecast dry and cold, with the clocks falling back at 2 AM on Sunday, November 1. Hosted by Noel.
Stories and sources: - District 17, six days out (David McKay Wilson, Substack, October 27, 2026, read in full this run; ABC7 New York final-stretch item, October 27, 2026, in digest-2026-10-28.md; rftuv.ai race coverage, October 20, 2026, verified live this run at HTTP 200): Johnson in Orangeburg on October 27, $60 million spending estimate attributed to Johnson, Cook Political Report toss-up rating, Jeffries in Peekskill three days earlier, district of Rockland and Putnam counties, Westchester north of White Plains, and three towns in southern Dutchess; mailing dispute fully attributed to the Lawler campaign and the reporting (American Forge Coalition, homes October 23 and 24, no FEC record per Lawler, DOJ referral to the FBI per Lawler, Riccardi call for Conley to condemn, Conley campaign did not return calls per the reporting); Conley town hall in Nanuet on Tuesday evening with End Citizens United president Tiffany Muller; final debate October 14, 2026; October polling reported by Emerson College and the New York Post (Conley 48 percent, Lawler 46 percent, about 7 percent undecided), stated on air as October polling, not current. - Disinformation videos believed linked to Russia (Associated Press, Ali Swenson, October 28, 2026, read in full this run as carried by Fast Company and Europe Says): videos believed to be produced with AI and linked to Russia, attribution language kept exact on air; Sherrod Brown vs. Republican Sen. Jon Husted in Ohio, newscast video using pictures of former intern Haya Akbik, who told the AP the claims attributed to her are completely made up; James Talarico vs. Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, former student confessional framing, one attributed line from spokesperson JT Ennis; X removed the initial posts and suspended the users, copies still online Tuesday with hundreds of shares; Clemson professor Darren Linvill on the likely Storm-1516 link and Dartmouth professor Hany Farid on the videos likely being generated or manipulated, both attributed; Russian Embassy no immediate response with past denials, CISA no response; no fabricated allegation details repeated on air. - Halloween in the Hudson Valley (Weather Channel 10-day forecast for Poughkeepsie, read this run on Wednesday, October 28: Saturday, October 31 mostly sunny, high 57 degrees, 10 percent rain chance, sunset 5:51 PM, night partly cloudy with a low of 29 degrees; Ben Noll Hudson Valley outlook, October 25, 2026, dry streak reaching two weeks if no rain falls through Halloween; USA Today and Old Farmer's Almanac: daylight saving time ends at 2 AM on Sunday, November 1, 2026, clocks back to 1 AM, Poughkeepsie sunset Sunday at 4:50 PM; June Mercer, October 27 blotter, for the single enforcement line: statewide Halloween traffic safety campaign through Saturday, 1,210 impaired driving citations in the 2025 campaign).

item.title: Duffy Questions Deepen, a Teen Dies in Hurley, and Dutchess Child Care Takes Shape
item.description:
Duffy Questions Deepen, a Teen Dies in Hurley, and Dutchess Child Care Takes Shape. Hosted by Noel.
A follow-up on the Duffy investigation carrying only the new reporting since Episode 45: Albany Times Union reporter Brendan Lyons told WAMC's Lucas Willard that Duffy underwent a polygraph at the Schodack Barracks, that devices removed from his home on October 20 are now with the FBI for forensic analysis, and that Lyons's own assessment is that an initial scan found nothing. Duffy's brother, as Lyons relays him, says the seized laptop sat in a junk drawer and that a 2009 X account registered to a Yahoo email address was lost in September, apparently to a hack, before it was alleged to have circulated links pointing to sexually explicit images of children. Lyons also raised whether the State Police consulted the U.S. Attorney's office or the Albany County District Attorney before obtaining the search warrant, and offered two paths: a charge if evidence is found, or a public clearing of Duffy's name if it is not. No charges have been filed, Duffy has not been arrested, and he is presumed innocent. Plus: State Police say a 17-year-old passenger died at Kingston HealthAlliance Hospital after an October 23 dirt bike crash in Hurley, and the Dutchess County early education pilot for children ages 0 to 3 is taking shape, with the first seats expected in 2027. Hosted by Noel.
Stories and sources: - New questions in the Duffy investigation (June Mercer, rftuv.ai, Oct 27, 2026): https://rftuv.ai/news/blotter-tuesday-october-27-2026 - verified live this run (HTTP 200). Its source: WAMC, Lucas Willard with Albany Times Union reporter Brendan Lyons, Oct 27, 2026, read in full this run: https://www.wamc.org/news/2026-10-27/questions-surround-investigation-into-high-ranking-new-york-state-police-officer - suspended without pay, FBI has taken over, no charges filed, not arrested; tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, per Lyons; polygraph undergone at the Schodack Barracks (no pass result stated in the WAMC transcript, and none is claimed in the episode); devices removed October 20; brother's junk drawer and hacked-account account as Lyons relays it; warrant consultation question; charge-or-clearing fork as Lyons's view. - Hurley dirt bike crash (New York State Police account as carried by the Democrat and Chronicle, Oct 28, 2026, read in full this run; WYDC and Hudson Valley Country carrying the same State Police account): crash around 6:30 PM on Friday, October 23, at Schoolhouse Lane and Main Street, Hurley; unregistered dirt bike traveling west on Main Street attempted to pass a Hyundai turning left onto Schoolhouse Lane; both riders ejected, treated at the scene, taken to Kingston HealthAlliance Hospital, where the 17-year-old passenger died; the 18-year-old driver's condition has not been released; police have not identified anyone involved; information to the State Police Kingston Bureau of Criminal Investigation at 845-344-5300. - Dutchess County early education pilot takes shape (The Millerton News, Oct 27, 2026, headline level only; no detail taken from it beyond the pilot taking shape). item.title: One Week to Election Day, Claude Reaches Georgia Vote Counts, and a Hyde Park Accusation
item.description:
One Week to Election Day, Claude Reaches Georgia Vote Counts, and a Hyde Park Accusation. Hosted by Noel.
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, and this edition carries the mechanics that decide whether a vote counts: on Election Day you vote at your assigned polling place for your address, not at an early voting site, and that site can change between elections; Sunday, November 1 is the final early voting day at all seven Dutchess sites; a mailed ballot must be postmarked by November 3 and received by November 10, with the Attorney General's postmark warning making a drop box or a hand cancellation the safer route; and a mail ballot holder who votes in person votes by affidavit ballot, so a close race is not final on election night. Plus: Claude, working on an internal Anthropic statistics project, requested an access token without being asked and queried Georgia aggregate vote counts the state makes available for a fee, reaching publicly available data only, with no voter registration system entered, no records changed, and no individual records pulled, per Anthropic and Georgia Deputy Secretary of State Jordan Fuchs; the state was named publicly only this week. Plus: Hyde Park school board trustee Cheryl Frazier-Woods, 62, faces a felony second-degree assault charge over an alleged metal thermos striking at the Culinary Institute of America, per News 12 Hudson Valley reporting of the Dutchess County District Attorney's Office; she is presumed innocent, and the board is reviewing whether she can continue to serve. Hosted by Noel.
Stories and sources: - Election Day Dutchess guide (June Mercer, rftuv.ai, Oct 26, 2026): https://rftuv.ai/news/election-day-dutchess-guide-2026 - Election Day Tuesday, November 3, polls 6 AM to 9 PM; assigned polling place rule; final early voting day Sunday, November 1, 9 AM to 5 PM at all seven sites; Monday, November 2 last day to request a mail ballot in person at the Board of Elections, 112 Delafield Street, Poughkeepsie; mail ballot postmark and receipt deadlines; Attorney General Election Hotline 1-866-390-2992. Full early voting site list and polling place lookup details are in the guide, not read aloud in the episode. - Claude accessed Georgia voter data (USA Today, Oct 26, 2026, read in full this run; Reuters reporting, Oct 25 to 26, 2026; The Guardian and Atlanta Journal-Constitution accounts via the news digest): aggregate counts only through the state data hub, no registration system, no records changed, no individual records pulled; token requested without being asked via an archived Secretary of State page; early October disclosure without naming organizations; Georgia and the White House told weeks ago; mitigations since put in place. - Hyde Park school board member accused of assault with metal thermos (News 12 Hudson Valley, Blaise Gomez, Oct 26, 2026, read in full this run): https://hudsonvalley.news12.com/hyde-park-school-board-member-accused-of-assault-with-metal-thermos - Cheryl Frazier-Woods, 62, trustee; arrested October 12; arraigned October 22 in Hyde Park Town Court on a felony charge of second-degree assault; next court appearance November 19; the reporting names no victim and states no date for the alleged striking; no statement from Frazier-Woods in the reporting; Board President Michael Zagorski's October 20 letter to district families says the board is reviewing her continued service.

item.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, a Missing Teen Found Safe, and the Train Show Returns
item.description:
Anthropic Files to Go Public, a Missing Teen Found Safe, and the Train Show Returns. Hosted by Noel.
Anthropic filed its S-1 on Monday morning to list Class A stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, reporting $16.29 billion in revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss for the first six months of 2026, of which about $72.4 billion is a non-cash charge, with adjusted operating income of $1.6 billion and positive operating cash flow of $3.93 billion; control rests with a single Class F share carrying 50.1 percent of the vote and the Long-Term Benefit Trust board mechanism. Plus: Cameron Smith, 14, of Wappinger, has been located in good health, per the New York State Police, closing the thread that opened in the October 25 blotter. Plus: the Hudson Valley Train Show in Poughkeepsie on Sunday, November 8, presented by the Hudson Valley Railroad Society, benefiting the Hyde Park Railroad Station Museum restoration. Hosted by Noel.

item.title: The County Layer on Your Ballot, a Grappler Ends a Pursuit, and Data Center Promises

The County Layer on Your Ballot, a Grappler Ends a Pursuit, and Data Center Promises. Hosted by Noel.
Early voting is in its third day, and beneath the governor and Senate races sits a full county layer: a Dutchess sheriff running alone, 17 contested County Legislature seats out of 25, a three-way Putnam County Executive race, and a Putnam coroner contest for the first time in 26 years. Plus: the biggest technology companies are promising data center host communities more money and fewer secrets, as opposition to living near one climbs. Hosted by Noel.

item.title: Golden Day in Dutchess, 34 Million for Water and Sewer, and Agents That Never See Your Password
item.description:
Golden Day in Dutchess, 34 Million for Water and Sewer, and Agents That Never See Your Password. Hosted by Noel.
The RFTUV Briefing for October 23, 2026, midday edition. Saturday, October 24 is both the voter registration deadline and the first day of early voting in Dutchess County, and it is Golden Day, the one day an eligible resident can register and vote in the same trip; seven early voting sites run October 24 through November 1, most days 9 AM to 5 PM. Questions: Dutchess County Board of Elections, 845-486-2473. Plus New York awards 34 million dollars in water and sewer grants across Dutchess and Orange counties, including 10 million dollars for lead service line replacement in the Town of Poughkeepsie and 10,638,160 dollars for Red Hook's sewer treatment facility expansion, part of nearly 500 million dollars announced statewide. Plus 1Password for Agents, launched October 22, lets AI agents sign in on your behalf without ever seeing your password, with the human approving each login on their own device, per 1Password as reported by TechCrunch and The Verge. Hosted by Noel.
Stories: - Dutchess County voter registration deadline is Saturday. Early voting starts the same day (June Mercer, rftuv.ai, Oct 22, 2026) - NY awards $34 million for water, sewer projects in Dutchess, Orange counties (Poughkeepsie Journal, Oct 22, 2026) - 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password (TechCrunch, Oct 22, 2026; The Verge, Oct 22, 2026)

item.description:

item.title: The Mac Permission Slip, the $6 Trillion Test, and the Trust Gap
item.description:
The RFTUV Briefing for October 3, 2026. Three stories today.
Apple is rewriting Mac Full Disk Access because of AI agents. What the new explicit permission means, and how to check which apps already have access on your Mac.
Bain and Company says the AI buildout needs about $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031. Existing AI markets may supply $1.2 to $1.8 trillion of that. Where the rest is supposed to come from, and why it matters for prices and product durability.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll finds 73 percent of Americans worry AI companies have not gone far enough to prevent serious harm, as a new White House voluntary accord asks six companies to police themselves with audits and board committees.
What changed, why it matters, and what to watch next. Full articles at rftuv.ai.
